title: Stacked voices
intro: The voices of B1 can stand on one another: *tanı-ş-* (reciprocal, to meet) → *tanış-tır-* (causative, to introduce) → *tanıştır-ıl-* (passive, to be introduced). This unit is about such stacks: the fixed order of voice suffixes, the causative passive *yaptırıldı* (it was had done, it was commissioned), the double causative *öldürtmek*, and voices with **can** and **can't**: *yapılamaz*, *yaptırılabilir*. Read a long verb from the root out and it falls apart into pieces you already know.

sections.title: Tanıştırıldım: reading a long verb from the root out

blocks.text: Voice suffixes always come straight after the root and always in the same order: the reflexive or the reciprocal first, then the causative, then the passive ([B1 unit 10](gp-passive), [B1 unit 11](gp-causative)). Negation and ability come next, then the tense, then the person.

blocks.label: The order of suffixes
lines: root + refl./recip. + caus. + pass. + neg./abil. + tense + person
yap-tır-ıl-a-ma-dı          it couldn't be had done
bul-uş-tur-ul-acak          they will be brought together

rows: to meet, to get to know each other

blocks.text: **How to read one.** Start at the root and add one suffix at a time, asking who does what. *Barıştırılamadılar* is *barış-* (to make peace) + *-tır* (someone makes them) + *-ıl* (that someone is hidden) + *-a-ma* (couldn't) + *-dı* + *-lar*: **they couldn't be reconciled**. The reciprocal makes two people act on each other, the causative brings in someone who makes it happen, and the passive hides that someone.

The reflexive takes part in stacks less often than the reciprocal, but the causative of a plain verb and then the passive is everywhere: *giy-* (to put on) → *giy-dir-* (to dress someone) → *giydir-il-* (to be dressed by someone).

items.en: I was introduced to Ayşe at a wedding.
The matter was discussed at yesterday's meeting.
items.note: *Görüşmek* (to meet; to discuss) + passive: a report in the style of the news.

items.en: The two old friends were finally reconciled.

items.tr: Mezunlar yirmi yıl sonra yeniden buluşturuldu.
items.seg: Mezunlar yirmi yıl sonra yeniden bul|uş|tur|ul|du.
items.en: The graduates were brought together again after twenty years.
The children were dressed early for the wedding.

blocks.title: Which passive after a causative?
blocks.text: A causative always ends in a consonant, so the passive after it is always `-Il`: *yaptır-ıl*, *boyat-ıl*, *bitir-il*, *göster-il*, *çıkar-ıl*. The *-n* and `-In` passives of [B1 unit 10](gp-passive) never follow a causative.
The order never changes: *yaptırıldı*, never *yapıldırdı*. To say that someone had a thing done, the causative comes first and the passive after it.

Causative + passive says that something was done because someone had it done, and keeps quiet about both of them: *Ev geçen yıl boyatıldı* (The house was painted last year: someone had it painted). With *tarafından*, the person named is the one who ordered the work, not the one who did it: *Süleymaniye Camii, Kanuni Sultan Süleyman tarafından yaptırıldı* (was commissioned by Süleyman), but *Mimar Sinan tarafından yapıldı* (was built by Sinan).

rows.en: he or she was kept waiting
you were kept waiting (plural or polite)

blocks.text: **Everyday causatives.** Many common verbs are causatives in form: *göstermek* (to show), *bitirmek* (to finish), *pişirmek* (to cook), *çıkarmak* (to take out), *düzeltmek* (to correct), *bekletmek* (to keep waiting). Their passives are causative passives too, and they are the everyday face of this unit: *gösterildi* (was shown), *bitirildi* (was finished), *pişirildi* (was cooked), *çıkarıldı* (was taken out), *düzeltildi* (was corrected).

**The person shown or taught.** With *göstermek* and *okutmak*, the person who sees or reads stays in the dative in the passive: *Misafirlere atölye gösterildi* (The guests were shown the workshop), *Öğrencilere bu kitap okutuluyor* (Students are given this book to read).

items.en: The house was painted last year (we had it done).

items.tr: Süleymaniye Camii, Kanuni Sultan Süleyman tarafından yaptırıldı.
items.seg: Süleymaniye Camii, Kanuni Sultan Süleyman tarafından yap|tır|ıl|dı.
items.en: The Süleymaniye Mosque was commissioned by Süleyman the Magnificent.
We were kept waiting for hours.
The guests were shown the workshop.
The mistakes were corrected in red pen.
The food was cooked over a wood fire.

blocks.text: French has the same layers: *Saçımı kestirdim* is **je me suis fait couper les cheveux**, and *Bu cami Kanuni tarafından yaptırıldı* is close to **cette mosquée a été construite sur ordre de Soliman**.

A causative can take a second causative suffix: after *-DIr* comes *-t*, and after *-t* comes *-DIr*: *öl-dür-t-*, *yap-tır-t-*, *oku-t-tur-*, *bekle-t-tir-*. In principle each suffix adds a person to the chain: someone has someone else make a third person act.

head: Verb
Causative
Double causative
rows: *okutturmak* (to have something read or taught by others)

blocks.text: **Where the second suffix counts.** When the first causative has become a word of its own, the second one brings back the extra person: *öldürmek* simply means **to kill**, so **to have someone killed** needs *öldürtmek*: *Padişah veziri öldürttü* (The sultan had the vizier killed), a sentence you will meet in Ottoman history.

**Where it doesn't.** In speech, *yaptırttım*, *kestirttim*, *yazdırttım* often mean no more than *yaptırdım*, *kestirdim*, *yazdırdım*. Careful written Turkish keeps one causative when no extra person is meant: *Saçımı kestirdim* (I had my hair cut).

items.en: The sultan had the vizier killed.

items.tr: Müdür bu kitabı bütün sınıflarda okutturdu.
items.seg: Müdür bu kitabı bütün sınıflarda oku|t|tur|du.
items.en: The head teacher had this book taught in every class.
I had my hair cut yesterday.
Who did you get to make this?

blocks.text: Don't add a second causative for emphasis in writing: *yaptırttım* in a formal letter reads as careless. One causative is enough unless a third person is really involved.

sections.title: Yapılamaz, yaptırılabilir: voices with can and can't

blocks.text: After the voices come negation and ability: `-mA`, `-(y)Abil` and `-(y)AmA` ([A2 unit 5](gp-ama-inability)), then the tense and the person. *Yap-ıl-abil-ir* is **it can be done**, *yap-ıl-a-maz* **it can't be done**, *yap-ıl-ma-malı* **it mustn't be done**. Notices, instructions and the news are full of them.

rows.en: he or she can be elected
you can be elected (plural or polite)

blocks.text: **Impersonal passives with can't.** Rules and warnings often put inability on the impersonal passive of [B1 unit 10](gp-impersonal-passive): *Bu kapıdan girilemez* (No entry through this door), *Bu ilaç reçetesiz alınamaz* (This medicine can't be bought without a prescription), *Buradan geçilemiyor* (You can't get through here).

**Participles.** The same stacks make useful adjectives: *yapılabilecek bir şey* (something that can be done), *Yapılacak bir şey yok* (There's nothing to be done), *kaçırılmaması gereken bir sergi* (an exhibition not to be missed).

items.en: This door can't be opened from the inside.
This problem can easily be solved.
The lost bag just couldn't be found.
The meeting can't be postponed.
The carpet can be sent for cleaning and be back in a week.

blocks.text: The passive comes before `-(y)Abil`: *Oraya otobüsle gidilebilir* (You can get there by bus), *gid-il-ebil-ir*. The order *gidebilinir* is sometimes heard but is not standard.

summary: Voice suffixes come straight after the root, in a fixed order: reflexive or reciprocal, causative, passive. Then negation or ability, tense and person: *tanı-ş-tır-ıl-a-ma-dı-k*.
After a causative the passive is always `-Il`: *yaptırıl-*, *boyatıl-*, *gösteril-*.
Causative + passive is **had done, commissioned**; with *tarafından* it names who ordered the work: *Kanuni tarafından yaptırıldı*, against *Sinan tarafından yapıldı*.
Everyday causatives make everyday causative passives: *gösterildi*, *bitirildi*, *pişirildi*, *düzeltildi*, *bekletildim*.
A double causative adds a person when the first causative is a word of its own (*öldürtmek*); in speech, *yaptırtmak* and *kestirtmek* often mean just *yaptırmak* and *kestirmek*.
Ability and negation follow the voices: *yapılabilir*, *yapılamaz*, *yapılamadı*, *yaptırılabilir*; with the impersonal passive they make notices: *Bu kapıdan girilemez*.
